synLogin

synLogin.Rd

Valid combinations of synLogin() arguments:

- authToken
- Profile-based authentication (from .synapseConfig)

If no login arguments are provided or only username is provided, synLogin() will attempt to log in using information from these sources (in order of preference):

1. .synapseConfig file (supports multiple profiles)(in user home folder unless configured otherwise)
2. User defined arguments during a CLI session
3. User's Personal Access Token (aka: Synapse Auth Token) from the environment variable: SYNAPSE_AUTH_TOKEN
4. Retrieves user's authentication token from AWS SSM Parameter store (if configured)

Usage

synLogin(email=NULL, silent=FALSE, authToken=NULL, profile="default")

Arguments

email

(str) Synapse user name (or an email address associated with a Synapse account)

silent

(bool) Defaults to FALSE. Suppresses the "Welcome ...!" message.

authToken

(str) A bearer authorization token, e.g. a personal access token.

profile

(str) Profile to use from .synapseConfig (default: "default").

Value

NULL

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
## Logging in
    library(synapser)

    # Logging in using a specific profile:
    synLogin(profile = "user1")
    # Prints: Welcome, username! You are using the user1 profile

    # Logging in with an authentication token:
    synLogin(authToken = "your_auth_token")
    # Prints: Welcome, username!
} # }
